sights.name: Lake Otome
sights.description: Emerald Lake Otome lies behind Kotogawa Dam, Japan's highest multipurpose dam.

sights.name: Yamanashi City Peach Blossom Land
sights.description: Peach orchards bloom like a pink carpet from early April, with rapeseed underneath.

sights.name: Mount Obina
sights.description: Mount Obina is a mountain in Yamanashi.

sights.name: Mount Ishimori
sights.description: This roughly 13-meter hill has about 3,000 azaleas that bloom in early May.

sights.name: Art Shop Message
sights.description: Opposite Fujiya Hotel at Fuefuki River Fruit Park, it offers a finger-drawn Mount Fuji pastel class.

sights.name: Mount Kojin Cherry Blossoms
sights.description: This spot features cherry blossoms and flowers on Mount Kojin.

sights.name: Kichijo-ji Temple
sights.description: A prefecture-designated Edo higan cherry called Shirakura spreads over the temple grounds.

sights.name: Wakuwaku Kanko Village
sights.description: Fruit farm near Fuefukigawa Fruit Park offering cherry picking from late April to late June, plus peach and grape picking in season; open 9:00-16:00.

sights.name: Ichigo Land
sights.description: Strawberry farm next to Fuefukigawa Fruit Park with six elevated-culture greenhouses where fruit is picked standing; open 9:00-16:00.

sights.name: Mount Kokushi
sights.description: A 2,592-meter Yamanashi 100 Famous Mountain named for Muso Kokushi's training legend.

sights.name: Mount Hafu
sights.description: Named for its roof-like shape from the south and often visited on an Okuchichibu ridge traverse.

sights.name: Mount Tokei
sights.description: This specialist-only rock peak near Nishizawa Gorge is named for its cockscomb-like summit rocks.

sights.name: Karisaka Mine
sights.description: Peak of 2,289 m northwest of Karisaka Pass, one of the Yamanashi 100 mountains, with southward views of Mount Fuji.

sights.name: Mount Kurogane
sights.description: A 2,232-meter Yamanashi 100 mountain with a distinctive pyramid shape.

sights.name: Mt. Kentoku
sights.description: Its highlight is a nearly vertical 20-meter chained rock face, with full summit views.

sights.name: Makioka Fruit Center
sights.description: Makioka Fruit Center is a fruit center.

sights.name: Koraku Garden
sights.description: Koraku Garden is a garden site.

sights.name: Kai Ya Nojo
sights.description: Grape farm with free picking of Kyoho and Shine Muscat and reservation barbecue, open daily 8:00-17:00 from about 20 August to early October.

sights.name: Jo Hisashi Sono
sights.description: Grape farm offering free picking of Kyoho and Shine Muscat, with an on-site museum of old farm tools; open 8:00-17:00.

sights.name: Roppo Pottery Gallery and Kiln
sights.description: This is a pottery gallery and kiln named Roppo.

sights.name: Nishizawa Gorge
sights.description: A top scenic gorge in Chichibu-Tama National Park, with waterfalls, rhododendrons, and autumn leaves.

sights.name: Yamanashishi Tami Hall
sights.description: Public hall inside Manriki Park, about 14 ha of pine and mixed woods beside the Fuefuki River; open 9:00-17:00, closed over the New Year.

sights.name: Seishi Yokomizo Museum
sights.description: The hall temporarily closed until August 22, 2021, under Yamanashi's COVID-19 request.

sights.name: Hizadate Tenno Cherry
sights.description: This Edo higan cherry, said to be 400 years old, is a prefectural natural monument.

sights.name: Otome Highland
sights.description: A 1,700-meter subalpine grassland in Makioka, known as a natural flower meadow.

sights.name: Firefly Village
sights.description: Manriki Park's Manyo Forest, along the Fuefuki River, hosts a June firefly viewing event.

sights.name: Oimatakubo Hachiman Shrine
sights.description: A shrine revered by Takeda Shingen and Nobutora, holding Japan's longest nagare-style main hall and oldest wooden torii.

sights.name: Tenjin Shrine
sights.description: Founding details are unknown, but Takeda Nobutora rebuilt the main hall, which retains a late Muromachi form.

sights.name: Tokuwa Valley
sights.description: A valley on the Tokuwa River with many waterfalls, about three hours from Kentokusan trailhead.

sights.name: Ichinokama Falls
sights.description: A suspension bridge leads to a 21-meter men's waterfall, with Kamazawa Falls and Medaki nearby.

sights.name: Manriki Park and Manyo Forest
sights.description: This 14-hectare city park along the Fuefuki River has a free animal plaza at its center.

sights.name: Otogatsuma Weeping Cherry
sights.description: A solitary hilltop weeping cherry in Makicho, with views of the Kofu Basin and Mount Fuji.

sights.name: Mount Kobushigatake
sights.description: Mount Kobushigatake, at 2,475 meters, is a Japan 100 Famous Mountain spanning Yamanashi, Saitama, and Nagano.

sights.name: Iijima Fruit Sightseeing Garden
sights.description: A fruit sightseeing garden.

sights.name: Tanba-en Garden
sights.description: Tanba-en Garden is a garden.

sights.name: Yamanashi City Community Exchange Center, Town Station Yamanashi
sights.description: It accepts service dogs and has wheelchair access, toilets, loaner chairs, first aid, and AEDs.

sights.name: Shimizuya Japanese Sweets
sights.description: Shimizuya is a Japanese sweets shop.

sights.name: Mitake Doun Tera
sights.description: Temple founded by Kato Mitsuyasu, with three yatsufusa plum trees that are a prefectural natural monument and over 200 mizuko jizo.

sights.name: Otakesan Nakatsu Shrine
sights.description: Founded as a Shugendo training site, its one-kilometer forest approach offers a quiet healing space.

sights.name: Temple Approach Plums
sights.description: Plum trees line a historic temple approach.

sights.name: Konara Yama
sights.description: Peak of 2,289 m northwest of Karisaka Pass, one of the Yamanashi 100 mountains, with southward views of Mount Fuji.

sights.name: Hirose Mizumi / Hirose Dam
sights.description: Dam lake at Hirose Dam, the first built among Yamanashi Prefecture-managed dams, viewed from a terrace in the adjacent park.

sights.name: Cherry Picking at Miyamoto Orchard
sights.description: Miyamoto Orchard offers cherry picking.

sights.name: Mount Oishi
sights.description: Mount Oishi has Oishi Shrine and a 12-meter granite rock said to be the prefecture's largest.

sights.name: Dai Chi Toge / Yume no Garden
sights.description: Mountain pass at 2,365 meters; a maintained trail of about 15 minutes leads to large granite formations named Yume no Garden, with Hakusan rhododendrons blooming in early to mid-July.

sights.name: Suntneige Wine Co.
sights.description: Meaning holy snow, Suntneige pioneered European grapes in 1953 and has won international awards.

sights.name: Tsuruya Brewing Co., Ltd.
sights.description: Tsuruya Brewing Co. is a brewing company in Yamanashi.

sights.name: Asahi Yoshu Soleil Wine
sights.description: Since 2002 the owner couple has made Soleil to bring out the grapes' full strength.

sights.name: Otome Mizumi Lookout [ Kon Kawa Damu ]
sights.description: Dam lake of Kotogawa Dam, a multipurpose dam on the Kotogawa River, which rises in 2,000-meter mountains of the Chichibu range.

sights.name: Takei Garden
sights.description: This site is Takei Garden.

sights.description: A 14-hectare urban park along the Fuefuki River in Yamanashi City, with a free-entry animal area.
